audit.whatIsWrong: Six of seven chart rows are already right; the two-item row is not. Both layers print Fiora, while whys[6] says 'Galio reclaims 2+ items off-lane', spikes[3] says his global R and W peel 'are why this stays even, not the 1v1', and late says the same again. The packet levelChart gives that row to Galio.
audit.why: The whole point of the last row on this page is that Fiora keeps winning the duel and stops mattering. Printing Fiora there erases the one thing the player needs to act on.
audit.corrected: win[6] and phases[6].side set to Galio at 4/10; phases[6].why rewritten to name the global ult and the peel.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[5].why says 'Ravenous Hydra is your spike — force fights the moment it completes' but no ultimate cooldown appears anywhere, and report[9] tells the player to commit on the level-6 spike without mentioning that Hero's Entrance is global.
audit.why: Hero's Entrance is 180/160/140s with 4000-5500 range. It is the reason this lane stays even despite a 1v1 Fiora wins, and it is the single number that should gate a dive: if it is up, the enemy jungler is effectively in the lane.
audit.corrected: The 180s global written into report[9].t; breakdown.spikes and breakdown.late rebuilt around it.

audit.whatIsWrong: report[5].t ends in the meaningless token 'Riposte his KA'. The full layer never gives a cooldown, and the three dontsFull bodies are identical filler under three different titles.
audit.why: This matchup has the cleanest Riposte interaction of any in the slice and the full layer does not state it: Justice Punch is a knockup — an immobilizing effect — so a parry that catches it returns as a STUN by Riot's own Riposte text. It is 11s at rank 1 over 650 range, against your 24s Riposte, so the trade is spending a long cooldown to delete a short one and that timing is worth stating. Shield of Durand is 18s at rank 1, soaks the burst and taunts on release, which is the reason to bait before committing R.
audit.corrected: report[5].t, breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0].d and dosFull[2].d now carry Justice Punch's 11s, its 650 range and the knockup-to-stun certainty; dontsFull[0..2].d rewritten to their own titles with Riposte's 24s, the Winds of War damage-over-time cloud, and Shield of Durand's 18s soak-and-taunt.
sources: enemyKit E text (knocking up) cd 11/10/9/8/7 range 650

audit.why: Two things I deliberately did not assert. First, wants.you[1] already tells the player the W taunt-release also converts the parry into a stun; whether a taunt counts as an immobilizing effect for that upgrade is not answerable from the kits, so I wrote the stun claim ONLY for the knockup and left the existing taunt line untouched. Second, whether starting the Shield of Durand channel before Riposte goes up beats the parry window is likewise unanswerable locally and appears nowhere in what I wrote. The mirror audit recorded both gaps.

notes: Cleanest matchup in the slice: the chart was right on six of seven rows and only the two-item row needed flipping, so nearly every edit went into putting real numbers and the real Riposte interaction into a full layer that had neither. Justice Punch is the one parry on this page that is a certainty rather than a maybe — it is a knockup, and Riot's Riposte text upgrades the stab to a stun when it blocks an immobilizing effect. I wrote that plainly. I did NOT extend the same promise to Shield of Durand's taunt, which wants.you[1] already claims; taunt-as-immobilize is not settled by anything local, so that existing string was left exactly as it stands.
